context.problem_statement: Find and remove duplicate records from a customer contacts table using SQL. Duplicates are defined as records with the same (email, phone) combination. Steps: (1) use GROUP BY + HAVING COUNT(*) > 1 to identify duplicate groups, (2) for each duplicate group, keep only the record with the most recent created_at timestamp using ROW_NUMBER() in a CTE, (3) DELETE the duplicate records (older ones), (4) report the count of duplicates removed, (5) validate the final table has no duplicates remaining. Also handle near-duplicates: find records where email matches but phone differs by examining edit distance.
context.expert_knowledge: Deduplication CTE pattern: WITH ranked AS (SELECT *, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY email, phone ORDER BY created_at DESC) AS rn FROM contacts) DELETE FROM contacts WHERE id IN (SELECT id FROM ranked WHERE rn > 1). Always verify with a dry run SELECT before DELETE. Near-duplicate detection uses Levenshtein distance or fuzzy matching. Consider soft delete (is_deleted flag) instead of hard delete for auditability.
